blog_summary: Adrian Colyer highlights this paper as an innovative approach to unsupervised learning of artistic styles using archetypal analysis. Unlike direct style transfer methods, the authors aim to uncover and represent artistic styles themselves as archetypes. The key insight is the use of archetypal analysis to decompose paintings into combinations of learned style archetypes, enabling both style synthesis and manipulation. The paper demonstrates how these archetypes can be visualized as textures and used to modify the style of images by adjusting the weighting of archetypes. The method leverages a pre-trained VGG-19 network to extract style descriptors, applies dimensionality reduction, and then uses archetypal analysis to learn a set of style archetypes. The results show promising applications in style interpolation and amplification, offering a new way to explore and manipulate artistic styles in a systematic and interpretable manner.
paper_title: Unsupervised learning of artistic styles with archetypal style analysis

Main Goal

In this project, we try to use an unsupervised learning approach i.e. archetypal analysis [1] to
automatically discover, summarize, and manipulate artistic styles from a collection of paintings
[3]. We learn archetypal representations of style from an image dataset of Van Gogh’s paintings.
